paper: Malashevich, Souza, Coh & Vanderbilt, New J. Phys. 12, 053032 (2010)
model: spinless simple-cubic 2x2x2 (8-site) tight-binding ordinary ME insulator (Appendix A, table A1)
quantity: linear orbital magnetoelectric susceptibility alpha_da = dM_a/dE_d
units: natural units e=hbar=c=1 (h=2pi); alpha in these units
berry_machinery_credit: adapted from gobel2024 Kubo/Berry kernel (shared-kernels-cache/gobel2024_sd_skyrmion_kubo_Lz_kernel.py): v=i[H,r], occupied-projector traces, eigenbasis Berry connections

kspace_chern_simons.note: smooth-gauge projection of delta trials at 2 lowest-onsite sites; eq (47a)

comparison.headline_claim: PBC k-space (Chern-Simons/axion OMP) linear ME susceptibility agrees with bounded-sample finite-field alpha.
comparison.assessment: Both formalisms implemented from scratch and run (<12s). Both yield alpha at the 1e-3..1e-4 noise floor for the accessible resolution (open clusters L<=5; k-grid 8^3). At this resolution the true (small) alpha signal is NOT resolved above numerical noise, so tight PBC-vs-bounded agreement to the paper level (differences ~1e-7 e^2/hc, requiring L=4..7 + 1/L,1/L^2,1/L^3 extrapolation on an 80^3 mesh) could not be demonstrated. The non-Abelian Chern-Simons integral is additionally gauge-sensitive on a coarse grid.
